approach: Use the movable-pulley constraint to find the pulley's acceleration from blocks 2 and 3, then use the fixed-pulley constraint to find block 1's acceleration.

steps.text: Take downward as positive. Block 3's acceleration is 6 m/s² downward and block 2's is 4 m/s² upward, so its downward value is −4 m/s².
The movable-pulley constraint makes the pulley's downward acceleration the average of the two.
The fixed-pulley constraint makes block 1's downward acceleration the negative of the movable pulley's.
A negative downward acceleration means block 1 actually accelerates upward.

common_mistakes.text: Taking block 1's acceleration in the same direction as the movable pulley instead of the opposite direction gives 1 m/s² downward, the wrong direction.
